text:
**The evidence does not establish whether the owner broke the law.** Satellite data detected 86.4 hectares of tree-cover loss in qualifying events after 2020: 81.3 hectares in 2021, 0.6 in 2022 and 4.5 in 2023. Most of those event areas were mapped as forest in the JRC’s 2020 reference.

Tree-cover loss alone does not establish who caused it, why it occurred, or whether it was lawful. A legal assessment would require information about the applicable rules, forest type, ownership and any permits or authorizations.
